paragraphs: Children in North Yorkshire who need a foster home are cared for by North Yorkshire Council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as the services shown above. Fostering for the council means looking after North Yorkshire children with its social workers and fostering support workers behind you; an agency assesses, trains and supervises its own carers and offers homes to children placed by councils, North Yorkshire among them.

The council said in April 2026 that, as of the previous September, its foster carers were providing homes for 438 North Yorkshire children and that more local foster families were urgently needed. Its guide describes a shortage of carers for older children and teenagers, and its fostering pages say it has more older children in care and fewer babies and toddlers. It asks for carers for brothers and sisters, teenagers and unaccompanied asylum-seeking children, for emergency, short-term and permanent fostering, and for short breaks for disabled children of at least three full days and nights a month. It is urgently looking for people with real experience of young people with challenging needs to become specialist carers for 16 to 18-year-olds, a role it advertises at over £840 a week in fees and allowances. It also runs No Wrong Door hubs in Harrogate and Scarborough, which bring fostering and residential care together and can suit people who work.

Pay for council carers rose by 3.4% for 2026-27. Our North Yorkshire allowance page sets out the weekly rate every carer receives for each child: £200.71 for under-fives, £228.68 for five to 10, £284.51 for 11 to 15 and £346.12 for 16 and over. Once accredited, carers are paid an age-related fee on top, from £72 to £126 a week, and advanced and specialist carers receive further skills fees. Birthday, festival and holiday allowances are paid as well, and the council offers £500 to newly approved carers.

Approval can take up to six months in two stages, the application and checks and then a full assessment, and new carers take seven training courses in their first year. Ask the council and two or three of the agencies above how they would support you where you live, and see the York, Middlesbrough, Stockton, Darlington, East Riding of Yorkshire and Lancashire pages if you are near the county's edge.
